## Repairs verified

The `--suggest` prime note now composes its seat through `render::seat` (`directory.rs:619-626`). The new HTTP test seeds a hostile persisted prime, exercises the actual directory recommendation producer, checks the exact safe note and separately confirms the structured prime value remains raw. This closes the previous `3bc726d` MEDIUM.

The directory drift line renders template names, versions, role and project. It emits a template-diff command only when the template/role names and project slug pass their grammars; otherwise it prints fixed raw-data guidance. Its unquoted dynamic command words are now strictly validated ASCII tokens without whitespace, quotes, metacharacters or leading hyphens, so they cannot become shell syntax/options. No raw key is placed in that executable suggestion.

`render::project` accepts 1-48 lowercase ASCII letters/digits in nonempty hyphen-separated runs. This matches the project-create slug and collision-suffix producers (`http/governance.rs:650-666,690-706`). Version strings are bounded digit tokens; JSON numeric versions cannot carry text framing.

The request list renders identities, states, role/instance address and reply; close reasons are escaped, capped and labelled as the closer's words. Output lists render identity/head/result/subject fields. Holding and lineage captions render role, instance and seat; drained request identities/replies, claims-list seats, reshape-prime and suggestion-role labels also render. These are display changes, not identity normalization or newly granted authority.

## Inventory disagreement and retained scope

The table calls `render_holdings` window name/reason safe because it is daemon-authored. That does not establish its data provenance:

1. Current assignment admission rejects `/` and edge whitespace, not internal newlines in an instance (`http/directory.rs:1198-1219,1436-1445`).
2. `window_name` concatenates that stored instance into `<project>:<role>-<instance>` without rendering. The receipt carries the raw name, including when the holder has no pane; the keep-first-holding reason also interpolates it.
3. `render_holdings` appends that name/reason directly after its newly protected holding caption. An allowed instance can therefore still introduce literal forged framing in CLI/tool-visible stdout.

This pipeline is unchanged in round five. It is a nonblocking preexisting residual in this delta verdict, not a claim of shell execution, changed tool-result authority or demonstrated model obedience. The new plain-receipt fixture contains no window object and does not cover this sink. Render the display name and any derived reason at the receipt presentation boundary while preserving the actual tmux name as data.

PM agreed and assigned this residual to F135: instance admission plus rendering legacy instance-derived receipt text and a hostile stored-instance regression. It is deferred work, not a repair certified at this head; no further #185 round is requested for it.

I also do not certify all `data.line` producers merely because their final formatter is reviewed: `render_requests` still returns such a line verbatim, and withdrawal builds one with the caller's reason (`http/requests.rs:302`). The list's fenced close reason does not change that separate command-receipt branch. Existing timestamp fallback and diagnostic/action prose remain producer-dependent.

F142 can retain the unchanged claims subject/release-reason and related free-text/line audit. Those fields are model-facing and not made trusted by being in a claims response. Likewise `whoami`/state/session results are model-facing data when read by an agent; own-seat provenance is not a general rendering guarantee. These qualifications do not establish a new round-five exploit.

Raw `--json` identities remain explicitly untrusted. Reading a note/template body intentionally exposes content; a fence is not semantic prompt-injection prevention or shell quoting. Prior F133/F134/F135 scopes are not globally cleared.
